Proton Pass (Proton Emergency Access) review: digital legacy verdict

Verdict: A solid privacy-first option: on any paid Proton plan you can name up to five emergency contacts who get access automatically after a wait time you choose, unless you deny the request. Best for: Proton users who want one emergency process covering Proton Mail, Pass and Drive.

Key facts

  • Category: Vaults & password managers
  • Pricing: Emergency Access is included on all paid Proton plans, including Proton Pass Plus. Check current pricing.
  • Best for: Proton users who want one emergency process covering Proton Mail, Pass and Drive.
  • Up to 5 emergency contacts
  • Wait time of 1, 2, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days

Official site / docs ↗

What are the pros and cons of Proton Pass (Proton Emergency Access)?

Pros

  • Up to 5 emergency contacts
  • Wait time of 1, 2, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days
  • You're notified of every request and can deny it
  • Covers your whole Proton Account, including emails, passwords and files

Cons

  • Both you and your contact need a Proton Mail address
  • Paid plans only
  • Longest wait time is 30 days

What are similar tools?

Vaults & password managers

Bitwarden

The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set.

Vaults & password managers

1Password

Excellent password manager, but it has no automatic emergency-access feature. Legacy planning relies on the Emergency Kit and family account recovery.

Vaults & password managers

Keeper

A solid choice with built-in Emergency Access: name trusted contacts who can request your vault after a wait period.
